title: Send a clear welcome packet the day a customer says yes
one_liner: When a quote is accepted or a contract is signed, an AI drafts a plain-language welcome email and a kickoff checklist so the customer knows what happens next and your team starts with everything in one place.
steps: A deal moves to 'Won' in your CRM, or a signed-agreement notice arrives; the customer record and scope notes are pulled together.
An AI step drafts a welcome email covering what happens next, what you need from them, and who their contact is.
The same step builds an internal kickoff checklist (items to collect, people to assign, dates to confirm) and creates the tasks in your task tool.
Whoever owns the account reviews the draft email, fills any gaps, and sends it; the tasks go live once they approve.
guardrail: The welcome email is saved as a draft and a person reads, edits and sends it; the AI never promises dates, prices or scope that are not in your signed agreement.
tools: Your CRM (HubSpot, Jobber, Housecall Pro or a Google Sheet), n8n or Zapier, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Gmail drafts, Asana, Trello or Google Tasks
prompt:
You are an onboarding coordinator for [business name], a [type of local business]. A customer just agreed to the work below. Write (1) a warm, plain-language welcome email draft and (2) an internal kickoff checklist. Use only the facts provided; if something is missing, write 'TO CONFIRM: [what]' instead of guessing. Do not invent dates, prices or promises.

CUSTOMER FIRST NAME: [first name]
SERVICE / SCOPE AGREED: [scope from the signed quote or contract]
START TARGET (if agreed): [date or 'not set']
WHAT WE NEED FROM THEM: [access, documents, photos, deposit, decisions]
THEIR MAIN CONTACT AT OUR TEAM: [staff name and phone/email]
TONE: [friendly and direct / more formal]

OUTPUT FORMAT:
EMAIL SUBJECT: ...
EMAIL BODY: under 150 words; thank them, say what happens next in 3 short bullets, list what we need from them, name their contact.
KICKOFF CHECKLIST: 5-8 items, each with an owner role ([office / technician / owner]) and a 'TO CONFIRM' flag where needed.
verification_note: Reasoned through the prompt with a sample scope (kitchen faucet replacement, deposit needed, start date not set): the output would be a short email with 'TO CONFIRM: start date' flagged and a role-assigned checklist; the explicit no-guessing rule prevents invented dates or prices. Placeholders only; no PII.

title: Get your holiday hours right everywhere from one sheet
one_liner: List your closures and special hours once, and an AI drafts the Google Business Profile special hours, website banner text, a customer post and a phone greeting line, ready for you to approve before the holiday rush.
steps: Keep one sheet of upcoming closures and altered hours (date, open time, close time, reason, on-call or emergency details if any).
Two weeks before each date, an automation reads the row and sends it to an AI model.
The AI drafts the profile special-hours entry, a short website banner, a social or email post and a voicemail greeting line, all using exactly the hours in the sheet.
You get the drafts in one email, check each against the sheet, then enter or publish them yourself.
guardrail: Nothing is published or changed automatically; a person confirms every hour against the sheet and enters the Google Business Profile special hours themselves.
tools: Google Sheets, n8n or Zapier, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Gmail, Google Business Profile
prompt:
You are the marketing coordinator for [business name] in [city]. Using ONLY the schedule below, draft customer-facing holiday hours messages. Do not add, change or assume any hours, services or promotions. If the sheet row is incomplete, reply with 'MISSING INFO: [what]' and stop.

HOLIDAY / EVENT: [holiday name]
DATES AFFECTED: [dates]
HOURS ON THOSE DATES: [open time to close time, or 'closed']
NORMAL HOURS RESUME: [date and time]
EMERGENCY OR AFTER-HOURS OPTION (if any): [phone or 'none']
TONE: [friendly / professional]

Write:
1. GOOGLE PROFILE SPECIAL HOURS: one line per date in the format 'Date: open - close' or 'Date: Closed'.
2. WEBSITE BANNER: under 20 words.
3. CUSTOMER POST (email or social): under 60 words, with the hours and a short thank-you.
4. VOICEMAIL GREETING LINE: one sentence under 25 words.
End with a one-line checklist of where to update: profile, website, social, phone greeting, booking page.
verification_note: Reasoned through the prompt with a sample (closed Thanksgiving Day, 9-1 the day before, normal hours resume Monday 8 a.m.): output would be four short items that repeat only the supplied hours, and the 'MISSING INFO' rule stops it guessing when a field is blank. Placeholders only; no PII.
